open_questions_resolved.wia_horizon_representation: RESOLVED (DELIVER decision, OVERRIDES ADR-106's literal `null` for WorkItemAge): WIA rows persist `Horizon = PercentilesOverTimeSnapshot.NoHorizon` (a named `public const int NoHorizon = 0;` on the entity), never NULL. Two hard reasons: (a) the unique index (OwnerId, OwnerType, MetricType, Horizon, RecordedAt) does NOT deduplicate rows whose Horizon is NULL — SQL treats NULLs as distinct — so WIA would silently accrue one duplicate row per refresh per day, breaking US-02 AC2 / DDD-5 'exactly one row per key per day'; (b) EF Core translates `s.Horizon == horizonParam` into `Horizon = @p`, which never matches NULL, so a null-horizon upsert predicate would always miss and INSERT instead of UPDATE. The column stays `int?` -> NO schema change and NO new migration. ADR-106 must gain an amendment note recording this at slice finalization (docs are a finalization activity, not a mid-slice one).
open_questions_resolved.wia_http_contract: RESOLVED (refines ADR-108, which says only 'WIA requested without a horizon'): relying on an omitted `horizon` to implicitly mean WIA is ambiguous against the already-shipped `[FromQuery] int? horizon` (an omitted horizon today is a legal CT call). Instead the change is ADDITIVE and EXPLICIT: add `[FromQuery] MetricType metricType = MetricType.CycleTime` to the existing `percentiles-over-time` action on BOTH controllers. Every existing CT caller stays wire-compatible byte-for-byte; WIA callers send `metricType=WorkItemAge` and no horizon, and the controller resolves the NoHorizon sentinel. No new route, no new DTO, no client/CLI/MCP version gate (ADR-108: 'reads inherit the existing MetricsController read gate; no RBAC change, no CLI/MCP client version gate').
open_questions_resolved.single_pipeline_no_second_recorder: RESOLVED (US-03 AC2 / Scenario 8 / KPI 'Pipeline reuse'): WIA recording is added INSIDE PercentilesOverTimeRecordingHandler. The existing `RecordAsync(..., Func<DateTime,DateTime,IEnumerable<PercentileValue>> readPercentiles, Action invalidateReadCache)` shape already accommodates the horizon-less WIA read — WIA is adapted as `(_, endDate) => metricsService.GetWorkItemAgePercentilesForTeam(team, endDate)`, ignoring the start date. What must be parameterized is the horizon set: CT loops [30,60,90], WIA runs exactly once with NoHorizon. Do NOT introduce a second handler, a second table, or a second endpoint — that outcome is precisely the slice's disproof condition in the learning hypothesis.
open_questions_resolved.cache_invalidation_must_survive: RESOLVED (non-negotiable regression guard): the handler's `finally { invalidateReadCache(); }` MUST remain and MUST cover the WIA read too. A slice-01 CI regression was caused by the recording handler warming the shared metrics cache mid-refresh; dropping/narrowing the invalidation breaks an unrelated @premium E2E. This is a standing ci-learnings rule: 'snapshot handlers reading caching metrics services must invalidate the cache'.
open_questions_resolved.demo_backfill_idempotency_signal: RESOLVED (subtle, catches a silent no-op): DemoPercentilesBackfillHandler's current idempotency guard is 'any snapshot with MetricType == CycleTime && RecordedAt < today -> skip'. If WIA rows are added under that same guard, every demo instance that already ran the slice-01 backfill will skip forever and NEVER gain WIA rows — the WIA tab would render empty in demo and screenshot E2Es while every unit test passes. The guard must become per-metric-family (evaluate the CT backdate and the WIA backdate against their own presence signals) so an already-CT-backfilled demo owner still gains WIA history on its next refresh.
open_questions_resolved.acceptance_harness_today_vs_syncday: RESOLVED (test-design constraint): PercentilesOverTimeAcceptanceTest anchors SyncDay to a fixed PAST date (2026-06-15 minus 90 days per fixture) for parallel isolation, while the recording handler writes `RecordedAt = DateOnly.FromDateTime(DateTime.Today)`. Recording-path assertions must therefore be expressed against real `DateTime.Today`, not against SyncDay; read-path seeding stays SyncDay-relative like slice-01. This is the same live/today blind spot already recorded for epic-5074 slice-08 — do not 'fix' the harness in this slice.
open_questions_resolved.effort_vs_slice_brief: RESOLVED: the slice brief reference-classes slice-02 at <=0.5 day ('pure reuse'). The decomposition below totals ~11h. The delta is real work, not scope creep: the FE selection model widens from a homogeneous numeric union to a heterogeneous one (threaded through model, service, hook cache key and widget), and the demo idempotency signal has to change shape. Track the variance as a reference-class learning at slice close-out rather than compressing the steps.

WIA percentiles are read via the already-existing ITeamMetricsService.GetWorkItemAgePercentilesForTeam(team, DateTime.Today) / IPortfolioMetricsService.GetWorkItemAgePercentilesForPortfolio(portfolio, DateTime.Today) — the service interfaces are NOT extended
NO second handler, NO second table, NO second event subscription is introduced; the CT horizon loop [30,60,90] and the single WIA write share one code path parameterized by horizon set
Same-day re-refresh overwrites the WIA row in place — exactly one WIA row per owner per day (DDD-5); a unit test drives two consecutive refreshes and asserts a single row

The handler's existing try/catch + structured Error log ('Percentile snapshot recording failed for {OwnerType} {OwnerId} ({MetricFamily})') covers the WIA path; a throwing WIA read does not break the refresh and does not prevent the CT rows already written from persisting

The existing `finally { invalidateReadCache(); }` is PRESERVED and covers the WIA read — a unit test asserts the invalidation still fires on both the success and the exception path (regression guard for the slice-01 CI failure and the @premium E2E it broke)
No EF migration is produced; `dotnet build` still emits zero warnings and `dotnet test` is green after the enum member is added

steps.scenario_name: Age percentiles are recorded by the same daily pipeline, not a second one (milestone-2 Scenario 8, driving-port half)
steps.implementation_notes: The existing `RecordAsync(int ownerId, OwnerType ownerType, Func<DateTime,DateTime,IEnumerable<PercentileValue>> readPercentiles, Action invalidateReadCache)` already fits WIA: adapt the horizon-less read as a lambda that ignores the start date, `(_, endDate) => metricsService.GetWorkItemAgePercentilesForTeam(team, endDate)`. What needs parameterizing is the horizon set — CT iterates the existing `Horizons` field, WIA runs once with `PercentilesOverTimeSnapshot.NoHorizon`. Reuse `UpsertSnapshot(ownerId, ownerType, horizon, recordedAt, percentiles)` and `ValueFor(...)` untouched; the upsert predicate must include MetricType so CT and WIA rows for the same day never collide. WATCH the RecordAsync parameter count — it is currently 4; adding a metric-type and a horizon-set parameter takes it to 6, still under the S107 limit of 7, so do NOT add a pragma. ci-learnings to pre-apply: constant arrays as `private static readonly` fields (CA1861 — a new WIA horizon array literal inside the loop is the classic trip); test helpers and private members declare CONCRETE return types (CA1859 — do not return IEnumerable<T> from a helper that builds a List<T>); use `Assert.EnterMultipleScope()` for consecutive asserts, never `Assert.Multiple`; `Has.Count.EqualTo(N)` for collection counts; `Is.Zero` not `Is.EqualTo(0)` (relevant for the NoHorizon assertions); `HandleAsync` must `await` `Save()` and never be `async void`; do not add a log-and-rethrow wrapper (S2139) — the dispatcher already swallows and the handler already owns its Error log. HARNESS CAVEAT: the handler writes RecordedAt from DateTime.Today, while the acceptance harness anchors SyncDay in the past — express recording assertions against real today. RED-by-skip: land the enum member + sentinel first so main compiles and stays green, then un-ignore the WIA handler tests one at a time.

steps.name: Additive metricType query param on both read endpoints + WIA series wiring + acceptance scenarios
criteria: Both `[HttpGet("percentiles-over-time")]` actions gain `[FromQuery] MetricType metricType = MetricType.CycleTime` — the ONLY signature change; no new route, no new DTO, no new controller
Existing CT requests (`?horizon=30`, no metricType) remain wire-compatible byte-for-byte — an acceptance test asserts a slice-01-shaped request still returns the identical CT payload

A WIA request (`?metricType=WorkItemAge`, no horizon) resolves PercentilesOverTimeSnapshot.NoHorizon and returns the persisted WIA series ordered by RecordedAt, side-effect-free (reads only the snapshot table, never a live recompute of historical days)

A WIA request that ALSO carries a horizon is not silently mis-served — WIA has no horizon dimension, so the horizon is ignored in favour of the sentinel and the response is still the single WIA series (documented in the action, asserted by a test)
An owner with no WIA snapshots returns an empty array — the honest empty-state contract the FE renders as D6 copy, never a zero-padded or broken series (US-03 AC3)

IPercentilesOverTimeSeriesQuery.GetSeries(ownerId, ownerType, metricType, horizon) is used as-is — the read port already carries metricType; only the controller's hardcoded MetricType.CycleTime goes away

Read-after-record acceptance scenario: a refresh is raised, then the WIA series is read back through the real HTTP surface and contains today's row — closes milestone-2 Scenario 8 end-to-end (US-03 AC2)
